findings.description: No server_side_encryption_configuration block is set, so objects in this bucket are stored unencrypted by default at rest, risking exposure of report data.
No 'acl' attribute is specified and there is no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block resource associated with this bucket, leaving access defaults unverified and potentially permissive.
The bucket storing ledger exports (financial data) has acl set to private but no server_side_encryption_configuration, meaning data is stored in cleartext at rest.
This bucket has versioning and logging configured but lacks a server_side_encryption_configuration block, leaving model artifacts unencrypted at rest.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined for this bucket, so operational runbook data, which may contain sensitive operational details, is stored unencrypted at rest.

The acl value 'lcatalogopts-delivery-write' is not a valid S3 canned ACL (likely a typo for 'log-delivery-write'). As written this will either fail to apply or produce an unintended/undefined access configuration on a bucket that holds sensitive audit-log data and is protected by a KMS key, undermining the intended access restriction; the risk is best characterized as broken/undefined access control rather than a confirmed grant of public write access, since there is no evidence the malformed string resolves to any actual permissive ACL.

The object is uploaded to reports_archive without specifying server-side encryption (kms_key_id or server_side_encryption), and since the destination bucket also lacks default encryption, this vendor roster file is stored in cleartext at rest.
